theater: 查科大草原與萬查卡山脈

battle.name: 查科戰爭
battle.theater: 查科大草原與萬查卡山脈
battle.brief: 一九三二年二月一日夜，巴拉圭軍奇襲北查科納納瓦與拉科拉哨所，沿查科鐵路步步推進，把戰線推向玻利維亞內陸；一九三五年兩役奠定勝負，玻利維亞主力師覆沒，六月簽訂和約。鐵甲艦屬十九世紀海上火力競逐的產物，查科遠在內陸，兩國水師僅餘內河炮艇，勝負全由步槍、機槍、輕砲與飛機決定。

kit.name: 鐵甲艦
kit.history: 木殼外面包了鐵。裝甲第一次比砲更難對付，砲塔的設計從此繞著它轉。

countries: 查科戰爭自一九三二年二月一日開打到一九三五年六月十二日簽署和約，交戰雙方是南美洲的內陸國玻利維亞與巴拉圭，戰場全在兩國接壤的查科地區。玻利維亞方面由拉巴斯政府主持，軍隊編制以師為骨幹，另有緊急徵召的民兵與後勤總局作戰補給樞紐，空軍隸屬國家海軍航空隊，由法國、美國、德國購置的轟炸機與戰鬥機組成，砲兵以七五公分野砲與一〇五公分野榴彈砲為骨幹；參謀部集中制訂作戰計劃，一九三二年下半年與一九三五年春季兩次大攻勢都由參謀總長主導。巴拉圭方面以亞松森政府為核心，一九三二年開戰時由胡安·埃斯特萬·古吉亞里執政，前線由查科軍總司令何塞·費利克斯·埃斯蒂加里布亞統一指揮，軍隊同樣以師為編制單元，並輔以大量騎兵與由平民徵集的民團；海軍雖無遠洋力量，卻有一支可沿巴拉圭河與帕拉納河活動的內河炮艇隊，後勤幾乎全部押在亞松森通往前線的查科鐵路上。玻利維亞在一八七九至一八八四年的太平洋戰爭之後失去海岸線，兩國海軍都只是內河巡邏隊，並無制海權可言。戰爭中阿根廷居間調解，並因領土事件一度與巴拉圭交惡；美國以仲裁者與軍火供應商兩重身份介入，巴西亦參與斡旋。雙方最高戰術目標其實指向同一片無價值的土地：北查科與萬查卡山脈一線。
countriesEn: The Chaco War ran from 1 February 1932 to the peace treaty of 12 June 1935, and the two belligerents were the landlocked South American republics of Bolivia and Paraguay, with all of the fighting taking place in the contested Chaco region along their common border. On the Bolivian side the government in La Paz directed the war; the army was organised around divisions, supplemented by emergency levy militia, with a logistics directorate acting as the hub of supply, and an air force attached to the national naval aviation branch, equipped with bombers and fighters bought in France, the United States and Germany. Field artillery was built around 75 mm guns and 105 mm howitzers. The general staff centralised operational planning, and both the great offensive of the second half of 1932 and the spring offensive of 1935 were directed by the chief of staff. On the Paraguayan side the government in Asunción was the hub, with Juan Esteban Guggiari in office when the war began in 1932; the front was under the unified command of José Félix Estigarribia, commander of the Chaco Army, whose force was likewise built around divisions and supplemented by a large cavalry arm and locally recruited militia. Paraguay had no ocean-going navy, but it did have a river gunboat flotilla able to operate on the Paraguay and Paraná rivers, and its logistics rested almost entirely on the Chaco railway running west from Asunción to the front. Bolivia had lost its coastline in the War of the Pacific of 1879 to 1884, so both navies were little more than river patrol forces, with no command of the sea between them. Argentina acted as mediator and, after an incident involving territory, was briefly at odds with Paraguay. The United States appears in the war in two guises, as arbitrator and as supplier of arms, and Brazil also helped broker a settlement. The strategic prize both sides fought for was in truth the same worthless land: the northern Chaco and the line of the Huanchaca mountains.
people: 玻利維亞一方的關鍵人物多出於軍人圈子。一九二八年以軍事政變上台的赫爾南多·西萊斯·雷耶斯任內推動查科石油開採與軍方的國界測量工作，卻在一九三一年下台；繼任的何塞·路易斯·特雷安·巴爾加斯面對仲裁失利與軍方要求開戰的壓力，最終在一九三二年批准動員。軍方核心是恩里克·佩納蘭達，他以參謀總長身分統籌查科戰役的兵員與物資，一九三五年十一月接掌國家元首；何塞·安東尼奧·阿蘭尼巴爾先後出任武裝部隊總司令，一九三五年敗局之中在克瓦特羅霍帕一役陣亡；參謀長恩里克·巴爾迪維耶索策劃了一九三五年春季的攻勢，卻在萬查卡山脈前碰壁而回。巴拉圭方面，何塞·費利克斯·埃斯蒂加里布亞以參謀長身分重整軍制、組建查科軍並全線指揮到一九三四年，戰後以將軍身分當選總統，一九四七年遇刺身亡；拉法埃爾·弗朗哥指揮的軍團在克瓦特羅霍帕與越過巴拉圭河的作戰中扮演主導角色，後來兩度出任總統；埃米利奧·霍索亞、卡洛斯·費爾南德斯等人分掌各師。除此之外還有大量不留姓名於戰史的角色：替美國石油公司測量地界的技師、隨軍記者、傳教士，以及在雨季裡為前沿車隊探路、補水並最終葬身查科的本地嚮導與車夫。
peopleEn: Most of the key figures on the Bolivian side came out of the officer corps. Hernando Siles Reyes, who came to power through a military coup in 1928, pushed the opening of the Chaco oil fields and the army's own survey of the disputed frontier during his term, but he left office in 1931. His successor, José Luis Terán Vargas, faced an unfavourable arbitration and mounting pressure from the military to take the field, and finally authorised mobilisation in 1932. The military core of the campaign was Enrique Peñaranda, who as chief of general staff organised the men and materiel of the Chaco war and took the presidency in November 1935. José Antonio Araníbar served as commander of the armed forces and was killed at the Battle of Cuatro Joppa during the disasters of 1935. The chief of staff, Enrique Baldivieso, planned the spring offensive of 1935 and was checked at the approaches of the Huanchaca mountains. On the Paraguayan side, José Félix Estigarribia reorganised the army as chief of staff, formed the Chaco Army and commanded the whole front until 1934; after the war he was elected president as a general, and was assassinated in 1947. The corps commanded by Rafael Franco played the leading role at Cuatro Joppa and in the crossing of the Paraguay river, and he went on to serve twice as president. Emilio Hosoya and Carlos Fernández among others commanded the individual divisions. Beyond them there is a host of people who left no names in the official histories: the surveyors who measured concession lines for the American oil company, war correspondents, missionaries, and the local guides and carters who prospected the road ahead of the supply columns in the wet season, drew water for them, and were buried in the Chaco.
kits: 卡面這件鐵甲艦建於一八六二年，是英國以木殼包鐵、旋轉砲塔與側舷重砲組合起來的產物，代表的是十九世紀中期以後以裝甲與重砲壟斷海權的技術世代。而查科戰爭是一場發生在兩國內陸的戰役，玻利維亞自一八八四年起便沒有海岸線，巴拉圭更是內陸國，兩國都沒有能投入戰場的艦隊；雙方的水上力量只餘內河炮艇。玻利維亞海軍在巴拉圭河與巴利維安河上有「胡馬伊塔」號等數艘武裝駁船，其中「胡馬伊塔」號據說是一九一一年在上海建造、一九三一年才由玻利維亞購入的舊式炮艇；巴拉圭的內河炮艇卻真正出了力，一九三三年十月它們溯帕拉納河而上，佔領阿根廷境內的佩雷斯·羅維拉島與塞里托島，一度引發阿根廷強烈抗議與外交危機。決定查科戰局的裝備全在地面：步槍以德製毛瑟九八式長短槍管步槍與阿根廷馬澤爾兵工廠製造的同型槍為主，機槍有德製施瓦茨洛澤 MG 08/15 與法製哈奇開斯式，砲兵用七五公分野砲與一〇五公分野榴彈砲，近距離支援靠八十一公分野迫擊砲與英製斯托克斯式火箭筒；玻利維亞另組成了規模極小的裝甲部隊，只有數輛輕型戰車與裝甲車，另有美製寇蒂斯「隼式」與法製波泰茲等飛機，巴拉圭則靠英製「費里狐狸」與法製布雷蓋 MB.150 建立空軍。真正把雙方拉開差距的既不是砲也不是槍，而是鐵路、卡車、汽油與飛機。與鐵甲艦同屬一個技術世代的，還有查科前線那些鋼筋混凝土碉堡群：萬查卡山脈的堡壘與博克龍要塞，本質上就是架在陸地上的裝甲帶，讓砲火打在混凝土上而自己繼續前進。
kitsEn: The ironclad on the card was built in 1862 and is the British product of a wooden hull sheathed in iron, revolving turrets and heavy broadside guns; it stands for the technological generation after the middle of the nineteenth century in which armour and heavy guns monopolised sea power. The Chaco War, by contrast, was fought in the interior of two countries. Bolivia had had no coastline since 1884, Paraguay is landlocked, and neither could bring a fleet into the theatre; all that remained of their sea power were river gunboats. The Bolivian navy had a handful of armed river steamers on the Paraguay and Ballivián rivers, among them the Humaitá, which is said to have been built in Shanghai in 1911 and bought by Bolivia in 1931. The Paraguayan river gunboats, however, did real work: in October 1933 they went up the Paraná and occupied the Argentine islands of Pérez Rovira and Cerrito, provoking a sharp Argentine protest and a diplomatic crisis. The equipment that decided the Chaco War lay entirely on the ground. Rifles were chiefly German Mauser Model 1898 in long and short barrel patterns and the same type made in the Argentine Mauser factory; machine guns included the German Schwarzlose MG 08/15 and the French Hotchkiss; artillery consisted of 75 mm field guns and 105 mm field howitzers, with close support provided by 81 mm mortars and the British Stokes rocket. Bolivia raised a very small armoured force of a few light tanks and armoured cars, and operated French Potez and American Curtiss Falcon aircraft, while Paraguay built an air force on the British Fairey Fox and the French Breguet MB.150. What really pulled the two sides apart was neither gun nor rifle, but railway, truck, petrol and aircraft. Contemporary with the ironclad was another thing the Chaco fighting produced: the reinforced concrete fortification line along the front, the blockhouses of the Huanchaca mountains and the fort at Boquerón, which functioned as an armoured belt on land, absorbing shellfire so that the troops behind it could keep advancing.
tactics: 巴拉圭的戰法是一條線上的推進加節點式的設防。查科鐵路自亞松森向西鋪設，一九二四年通到馬西塞爾·埃斯蒂加里布亞，戰時繼續伸長；前線車站往前挪一格，砲兵營與步兵營就往後挪一格。步兵以營為最小作戰單位，縱隊行軍，兩翼以騎兵巡邏，炮火準備後以短距離迅猛突進佔領據點，佔領後立即構築野戰陣地、架設野戰電話線，把鐵路末端變成新的出發點。一九三二年二月一日夜裡對納納瓦與拉科拉哨所的奇襲，靠的是切斷電報線與夜間接近；五月至六月包圍博克龍要塞時，靠的是砲火封鎖與切斷外圍交通，最終讓守軍全滅。玻利維亞的戰術在頭兩年以機動為主：一九三二年春夏在坎迪納方向發動反攻，一度收復失地；一九三四年起改為依托萬查卡山脈的鋼筋混凝土堡壘群作長期防禦，以交通壕與障礙區把對方牽制在山前，再趁對方攻勢疲憊時集中一、兩個師在隘口實施反衝鋒。然而隘口反衝鋒需要炮火優勢與指揮協同，一旦連續數次失利，陣地便難以維持。空軍是另一端的槓桿：玻利維亞靠飛機把補給與傷兵從拉巴斯、科恰班巴與聖卡洛斯直接送到前線，減少對地面公路的依賴；巴拉圭則靠鐵路把人和彈藥送到彈著點，再用空軍掩護地面推進。地形與季節決定攻勢窗口：查科北部是大片平坦的灌叢與仙人掌地，雨季十二月至二月車輛與重砲幾乎寸步難行，雙方真正大打出手的是五月至次年三月這段旱季；一九三五年三月的攻勢正趕在乾季末段，公路勉能通行，裝甲車才得以發揮作用。
tacticsEn: The Paraguayan method was an advance along a single line combined with fortifying each node in turn. The Chaco railway ran west from Asunción, reached Mariscal Estigarribia in 1924 and was extended during the war: whenever the forward station moved one stage, the artillery and infantry trains moved one stage behind it. The battalion was the smallest tactical unit for the infantry, which marched in column, patrolled its flanks with cavalry, and after preparatory fire charged over short distances to seize its objective; on taking the ground it at once dug field positions and strung field telephone wire, converting the end of the railway into a new start point. The night attack on the Nanawa and La Koroga outposts on 1 February 1932 depended on cutting the telegraph line and closing in under cover of darkness; the encirclement of the fort at Boquerón between May and June relied on artillery blockade and on severing the roads behind the garrison, and ended with the defenders wiped out. Bolivian tactics in the first two years were mobile: in the spring and summer of 1932 they counter-attacked in the Kandina direction and briefly recovered lost ground; from 1934 they changed to a long defensive holding on the reinforced concrete blockhouses of the Huanchaca mountains, using entrenchments and obstacle zones to pin the enemy in front of the ridge and then concentrating one or two divisions for a counter-stroke at the passes. Such a counter-stroke needed artillery superiority and command coordination; once it failed several times running, the positions could no longer be held. Air power was the lever at the other end. Bolivia used aircraft to fly ammunition and wounded men straight from La Paz, Cochabamba and Santa Cruz to the front, cutting its dependence on the road; Paraguay moved men and shells forward by train to the firing line and used its air force to cover the ground advance. Terrain and season fixed the window for offence. Northern Chaco is flat country of scrub and cactus, and in the wet season from December to February vehicles and heavy guns could scarcely move; the real battles of the war were fought in the dry season from May to March. The offensive of March 1935 came at the end of that dry season, when the roads were barely passable and armoured cars could still make their contribution.
data: 這場戰爭的時間跨度是三年四個月又十一天，自一九三二年二月一日打到一九三五年六月十二日簽訂和約。空間尺度上，前線由北查科的納納瓦與博克龍一帶（南緯約二十二度五分）一路推到巴拉圭河西岸的康塞普西翁（南緯約二十一度），推進距離超過兩百公里；查科鐵路的鋪設總長接近一千公里，公路與空運線更長。兵力上，玻利維亞自一九三二年起以徵召制把全國壯丁分批送上戰場，先後動員約五萬至八萬人，巴拉圭則集中使用常備軍與民兵，動員約三萬至五萬人；前線同時作戰的部隊通常以師為單位，關鍵會戰中投入的兵力多在數千人至一萬人之間。損失方面，各方統計口徑出入很大，一般說法是玻利維亞陣亡約五千至一萬人、受傷約一萬至一萬八千人，巴拉圭陣亡約三千人、受傷約一萬人上下，合計傷亡在數萬人量級；一九三二年六月博克龍要塞的守軍約一千人幾乎全滅，最後突圍者不足百人。空軍方面，玻利維亞先後得到約三十至五十架作戰飛機，多為法製波泰茲系列與美製寇蒂斯隼式，巴拉圭初期只有十餘架老舊機型，後來購進法製布雷蓋 MB.150 與英製費里狐狸等數十架，據戰史記載，一九三四年七月一日曾爆發一次空戰並有玻利維亞戰機被擊落。土地方面，一九三八年經美國總統仲裁，最終劃給巴拉圭的面積約十一萬六千平方公里，多屬無人居住的荒原。
dataEn: The war lasted three years, four months and eleven days, from 1 February 1932 to the signature of the peace treaty on 12 June 1935. In space, the front ran from the Nanawa and Boquerón sector of the northern Chaco, at about 22.5 degrees south, all the way to Concepción on the west bank of the Paraguay river at about 21 degrees south, a distance of more than two hundred kilometres; the Chaco railway was laid for close to a thousand kilometres, and the road and air routes were longer still. In manpower, Bolivia used its levy system from 1932 to send men to the front in batches, mobilising something between fifty and eighty thousand men over the war, while Paraguay drew on its regular army and militia and mobilised perhaps thirty to fifty thousand; the units actually engaged at any one time were usually divisions, and the forces committed to the decisive actions ran from several thousand men to about ten thousand. Casualty figures differ widely between sources, but the usual account is that Bolivia lost about five to ten thousand dead and perhaps eleven to eighteen thousand wounded, and that Paraguay lost around three thousand dead and some ten thousand wounded, putting the combined cost in the tens of thousands; in June 1932 the roughly one thousand men garrisoning the fort at Boquerón were virtually annihilated, fewer than a hundred breaking out. In the air, Bolivia eventually received roughly thirty to fifty combat aircraft, mostly French Potez types and American Curtiss Falcons, while Paraguay started with a dozen obsolete machines and later bought dozens of French Breguet MB.150s and British Fairey Foxes; the official histories record an air engagement on 1 July 1934 in which a Bolivian aircraft was shot down. As for land, the award made by the President of the United States in 1938 finally gave Paraguay some 116,000 square kilometres, the greater part of it uninhabited scrub.
cause: 打起來的根由是三十年代以來查科地區的邊界與石油糾紛。玻利維亞與巴拉圭的國界自一八七四年和約起便含混不清，一九二一年由阿根廷總統伊里戈延仲裁的結果偏向巴拉圭，一九二八年柯立芝政府任命的仲裁裁決又把爭議地的大半判給巴拉圭，玻利維亞始終不承認那條線。真正的引爆點是石油：一九二四年美孚系公司取得玻利維亞查科北部的開採租讓權，一九二五年開始產油，並計劃築一條通往阿根廷的輸油管把原油送出去；玻利維亞政府急於把查科變成財政支柱，巴拉圭則擔心自己的地盤被瓜分。接著是鐵路：一九二〇年代巴拉圭把查科鐵路一路往西鋪到邊界附近，玻利維亞指其為侵略的前奏，巴拉圭堅稱只是經濟開發，兩國關係因此急劇惡化。邊境上的零星衝突不斷累積，一九二九年十二月科隆尼亞·奧多涅斯聚落一樁女孩被殺的案件被雙方拿來指責對方，一九三一年冬兩國邊防隊在邊界哨所之間再度交火。國際環境同樣推了一把：一九二九年大蕭條令玻利維亞的礦產出口崩跌，政府想用石油撐住財政；一戰後各國堆積的過剩軍火源源不斷流入拉美，兩國內部都有一股「用一場勝仗解決一切」的風氣。玻利維亞軍人政權需要勝利來鞏固合法性，巴拉圭則要在國勢低潮中重振國族自信，於是一九三二年二月，兩支部隊在納納瓦互相開火。
causeEn: The quarrel that started the war was a tangle of frontier and oil in the Chaco during the 1930s. The Bolivian-Paraguayan border had been vague since the peace treaty of 1874; the arbitration of 1921 by the Argentine President Yrigoyen went against Bolivia, and the award made in 1928 by an arbitrator appointed by the Coolidge administration again handed the greater part of the disputed ground to Paraguay, a line Bolivia never accepted. The true flashpoint was oil. In 1924 a Standard Oil affiliate secured the concession to the northern Chaco of Bolivia; production began in 1925, and a pipeline to Argentina was planned to carry the crude out. The Bolivian government was in a hurry to turn the Chaco into a source of state revenue, while Paraguay feared that its own territory was about to be carved up. The railway came next: in the 1920s Paraguay pushed its Chaco line west towards the border, which Bolivia called the prelude to an invasion and which Paraguay insisted was nothing but economic development, and relations between the two deteriorated sharply. Minor clashes on the frontier kept accumulating; the killing of a girl at the Colonia Oddóñez settlement in December 1929 was used by each side to accuse the other, and in the winter of 1931 border guards again exchanged fire between outposts. The international setting pushed just as hard. The crash of 1929 had ruined Bolivia's mineral exports, and the government looked to oil to steady the treasury; surplus First World War munitions were flowing into Latin America, and in both countries there was a wind of opinion that one decisive victory would settle everything. Bolivia's military regime needed a victory to legitimise itself, and Paraguay needed to rebuild national confidence in a time of national weakness, so in February 1932 the two forces opened fire at Nanawa.
impact: 戰爭結束時玻利維亞丟掉了查科北部，土地、石油收入與戰前的設想一起破滅，財政靠借貸與加稅硬撐，軍隊被消耗到骨子裡，前線的慘狀成了全國性的創傷記憶，中部高原與高地少數族裔的徵召兵更是首當其衝。這種挫敗在政治上直接引發了對軍人政權的不滿，一九三八年玻利維亞正式放棄對查科的主張，一九五二年爆發革命推翻掌權三十年的軍人文官集團，隨後的國有化與土地改革把石油與大莊園收歸國家，軍隊也從此走向專業化。巴拉圭則得到十一萬平方公里以上的土地，但多數是無水無路的荒原，無法變成農業與牧業的產出，全國面積增加約四分之一，總人口卻不足一百萬，國家機器被軍隊與地界糾紛撐得極度膨脹。查科老兵成為一支獨立的政治軍團：一九四七年他們推翻岡薩雷斯政府，之後「查科派」在內政與對外政策上長期占上風，一九四九年拉法埃爾·弗朗哥上台後，雙方關係仍因河權與炮艇爭議而緊張，直到一九五〇年代與六〇年代才逐漸降溫。軍事技術上，這場戰爭被各國參觀團寫進了課本：機關槍與輕型高射砲對密集步兵的毀滅性、空軍對地面補給的價值、公路與鐵路對作戰節奏的支配，都說明傳統兵站戰已被機械化作戰取代。戰場上留下的無主墳塚被稱為「查科空地」，從空中仍可辨認出成片的墳墓標記，成為南美洲最有名的戰爭紀念地之一。
impactEn: When the war ended Bolivia had lost the northern Chaco, and with it the land, the oil revenue and the future it had been built around; the treasury was held together by borrowing and new taxes, the army was spent to the bone, and the condition of the front became a national trauma, with the conscripted men of the central highlands and the indigenous communities suffering first and worst. That defeat fed directly into the political unravelling of the military regime: in 1938 Bolivia formally renounced its claim to the Chaco, and in 1952 a revolution brought down a civilian-military oligarchy that had ruled for thirty years; the nationalisation and land reform that followed placed the oil and the great estates in the hands of the state, and the army turned professional. Paraguay received more than 116,000 square kilometres, but most of it was waterless, roadless scrub that could be turned into neither crops nor grazing, so that national territory grew by roughly a quarter while the population remained under a million, and the state apparatus was inflated by an army and by a running border dispute. The veterans of the Chaco became an independent political corps: they overthrew the González government in 1947, and the Chaco faction dominated politics and foreign policy for years afterwards. After Rafael Franco took power in 1949 relations with Bolivia stayed tense over river rights and gunboats, and only cooled during the 1950s and 1960s. Technically the war was written into the textbooks of every observing mission: the destructiveness of machine guns and light anti-aircraft guns against massed infantry, the value of aviation to ground supply, the dominance of road and rail over the rhythm of operations, all of which showed that the old war of marching armies had been overtaken by mechanised war. The mass of unburied dead left on the field is known as the empty space of the Chaco, and its grave markers can still be picked out from the air, making it one of the best known war memorials in South America.
result: 結果是巴拉圭完勝而玻利維亞一敗塗地。一九三五年一月伊比庫伊一役，巴拉圭突破玻利維亞在查科南緣的防線；二月康塞普西翁方向再取一城；三月初的庫魯亞蒂戰役中，巴拉圭集中優勢砲兵，對玻利維亞在邁蒙平原上的防線實施密集火力準備後以步兵突進，玻利維亞一個整師當場崩潰；四月的克瓦特羅霍帕一役，玻利維亞最後一個整師被殲滅，總司令陣亡；四月十四日巴拉圭部隊越過巴拉圭河進入玻利維亞本土，五月初兵臨康塞普西翁，玻利維亞政府連夜遷都科恰班巴。一九三五年六月一日玻利維亞請求停火，雙方在布宜諾斯艾利斯談判，於六月十二日簽署和約：玻利維亞承認巴拉圭對查科大部分地區的主權，只保留沿巴拉圭河與查科河下游的一條走廊，並同意由阿根廷、巴西與美國等國組成委員會勘定邊界。一九三八年，美國總統仲裁最終把約十一萬六千平方公里的土地判給巴拉圭，玻利維亞同年放棄索賠。和約簽得很快，麻煩卻留了下來：雙方都明白，玻利維亞失去的不只是一塊空地，而是把它拖入現代國家的那口油井；巴拉圭得到的也只是一片無法耕種的荒原，反而養出一支好戰的軍隊。往後十餘年，巴拉圭河航行權與內河炮艇的歸屬反覆成為爭議，一九三九年玻利維亞向巴西購入兩艘內河炮艇時巴拉圭提出強烈異議，兩岸關係再度緊張，直到一九七〇年代仍有衝突，邊界與河權問題則一直拖到二十世紀末才由條約收束。
resultEn: The result was a complete Paraguayan victory and a Bolivian catastrophe. At Ybycuí in January 1935 Paraguay broke the Bolivian line on the southern edge of the Chaco; in February another town fell in the direction of Concepción; in the opening days of March, in the Battle of Kuruyaty, Paraguay massed superior artillery and, after a dense preparation against the Bolivian line on the plain, sent its infantry forward, and an entire Bolivian division dissolved on the spot. In April, at Cuatro Joppa, the last Bolivian division in being was annihilated and its commander killed; on 14 April Paraguayan troops crossed the Paraguay river into Bolivian territory, and by the beginning of May they stood before Concepción, the Bolivian government moving the capital to Cochabamba overnight. Bolivia asked for a ceasefire on 1 June 1935; the two sides negotiated in Buenos Aires and on 12 June signed a peace treaty under which Bolivia recognised Paraguayan sovereignty over the greater part of the Chaco, keeping only a corridor along the Paraguay and Chaco rivers, and agreeing to a commission of Argentina, Brazil and the United States to fix the boundary. In 1938 an arbitral award by the President of the United States finally gave Paraguay some 116,000 square kilometres, and Bolivia renounced its claims in the same year. The treaty came quickly; the trouble was left behind. Both sides understood that Bolivia had not lost only a piece of empty ground but the oil well that was to have made it a modern state, and that Paraguay had gained only a stretch of country it could not farm, which instead bred a martial army. For more than a decade afterwards the navigation of the Paraguay river and the ownership of the river gunboats remained a recurring dispute; when Bolivia bought two gunboats from Brazil in 1939 Paraguay lodged a vigorous protest and relations deteriorated again, and clashes were still occurring in the 1970s, while the border and river rights questions were not settled by treaty until the end of the twentieth century.
